newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Treasury okays Cargill food export to N.Korea.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Treasury okays Cargill food export to N.Korea.

text.p: The U.S. Treasury has given a Minneapolis firm permission to export 500,000 tonnes of food to North Korea, a U.S. official said on Monday, a week after the Communist nation apologised for a submarine incursion into South Korean waters.

The official, who spoke on condition of anonymity, said permission was given to Cargill Inc., one of the world's largest private grain traders, to make the export in a barter transaction with famine-struck North Korea.

Cargill Spokeswoman Laurie Johnson declined to say if the company was interested in such a barter deal. She said the license to export the food to North Korea had been approved on Dec. 30 in response to an application submitted by Cargill in September to sell North Korea up to 2 million tonnes of grain.

"We have received a license to export up to 500,000 tonnes of food, consisting of wheat and or rice," Johnson told Reuters. "We probably will not have much more to say about this, as a courtesy to the customer."

North Korea last week apologised for an incursion by one of its submarines into South Korean waters, an unprecedented step welcomed by the Clinton administration as a "significant development" toward reducing tensions on the Korean peninsula.

North Korea also has expressed willingness to discuss its nuclear fuel programme and a framework for regional peace talks. The United States has said it considers North Korea's nuclear programme one of the main threats to peace in East Asia and has pressured the communist state through a trade embargo and other methods to open up its facilities for inspections.
The official North Korean news agency KCNA said on Dec. 30 that the United States had pledged to ease the trade embargo against North Korea.
Cargill is active in all major commodities including metals, soft commodities, meats, salt and many others.

North Korea has suffered from famine after two years of serious flooding and the United States gave $2 million last February to help alleviate the famine. The State Department at the time said the U.S. Agency for International Development would grant the money to the United Nations World Food Programme to buy the food for North Korea.
